The day Keerthana's promotion to shift lead was pinned on the notice board of the Chennai call centre, Tenzin stopped saving her a seat in the canteen. They had trained together, covered each other's breaks, shared auto fares home for two years.
Keerthana felt the chill like a draught. She didn't post about the promotion. She also didn't say sorry for it.
At the Friday team meeting she said, "Half of what I know about calming angry callers, I learned from Tenzin's desk." Tenzin looked up, surprised, then looked away.
Keerthana kept things simple after that: a "good morning", a samosa left on Tenzin's desk on a long day, no pressure to talk. She guessed the distance might be about losing their old evenings together, not about hating her.
In the third week, Tenzin sat down across from her at lunch. "Pass the pickle."

"Sangeeta, it's Sachin. Can I come up? I brought the lunch you like from the canteen."
"You don't have to do this."
"I know." He set the tiffin on her dining table. "Three of us have forwarded your profile. The design head at Karan's firm wants to talk on Monday."
Sangeeta stared at the tiffin. "I feel like a charity case."
"Were you a charity when you rewrote my entire portfolio last year? For free, on a Sunday?"
"That was different."
"How?"
She didn't have an answer. She opened the tiffin. Aloo parathas, still warm.
"Okay," she said quietly. "Monday. Thank you."
"And when you're heading a design team somewhere, you'll do the same for someone else."
"I will." She tore a paratha in half and passed it to him. "Sit. Eat with me."

qa.q: When does the design head at Karan's firm want to talk?
qa.a: On Monday.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling when she said "I feel like a charity case"?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and small, uncomfortable accepting help after losing her job.

qa.q: What changed Sangeeta's mind about accepting the help?
qa.a: Sachin reminded her that she had rewritten his portfolio for free, showing that help between coworkers goes both ways.

qa.q: How does Sachin see his visit?
qa.a: Sachin sees it as returning a favour and keeping their working friendship human, not as pity.

grounding: A laid-off protagonist receives referrals and a shared lunch from coworkers and learns to accept help without feeling small.
